```{r}
#| label: setup
## Everything this memo needs was saved by the memo_draft target (data/memo_inputs.rds);
## only base R and knitr are used so the memo renders outside the project's renv
m <- readRDS("data/memo_inputs.rds")

## Percent with one decimal ("0.3%"), and "<0.1%" for tiny values
pct <- function(x, digits = 1) ifelse(x < 10^-(digits + 2), paste0("<", 10^-digits, "%"), paste0(formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = digits), "%"))

## "A, B and C"
and_list <- function(x) if (length(x) <= 1) x else paste(paste(head(x, -1), collapse = ", "), "and", tail(x, 1))
```

## Executive summary

- **`r m$headers$overall`.** The highest risk of Rift Valley fever outbreaks in `r m$meta$period_label` is concentrated in `r and_list(m$risk$top_countries_text)`. [CONTEXT]
- **`r m$headers$relative`.** `r m$relative$n_never` of the `r m$relative$n_compared` medium- and high-risk locations are forecast to be at their highest risk since `r m$relative$history_start_text`, mostly in `r and_list(m$relative$top_never_countries)`. [CONTEXT]
- **`r m$headers$countries`.** The chance that at least one outbreak is recorded is highest in `r and_list(m$countries$top3_text)`. [CONTEXT]
- **`r m$headers$expected`.** [CONTEXT]
- **`r m$headers$unexpected`.** [CONTEXT]

## Introduction

Each month we forecast the chance of Rift Valley fever outbreaks being recorded across Africa, using a machine-learning model of weather and weather forecasts, vegetation, livestock, land cover and estimated herd immunity, trained on outbreaks reported to WOAH (WAHIS) since 2007. This memo covers `r m$meta$period_label` and uses data available on `r m$meta$forecast_date_text`.^[The forecast is for outbreaks starting `r m$meta$window_days_text` after `r m$meta$forecast_date_text` (`r m$meta$window_dates_text`). Outbreak records used run to `r m$meta$outbreak_data_end_text`. Model: `r m$meta$model_id`, trained `r m$meta$training_run_text`.]

## `r m$headers$overall`

[DESCRIPTION OF FIGURE 1.] This month, `r m$risk$n_high` locations are rated high risk and `r m$risk$n_medium` medium risk.^[Risk levels compare this forecast with our model's predictions across the model test period (`r m$risk$test_period_text`). A "High" risk marks locations in the top `r m$risk$high_top_pct` of all predicted probabilities over this test period. Across the test period, "High" risk hexes (as defined here) had outbreaks at `r m$risk$high_lift` times the average rate and accounted for `r pct(m$risk$high_share, 0)` of recorded outbreaks. "Medium" risk marks the top `r m$risk$medium_top_pct`, which captured `r pct(m$risk$medium_share, 0)` of recorded outbreaks.]

![Forecast risk of a Rift Valley fever outbreak in `r m$meta$period_label`. Thick outlines: locations where the model has anticipated past outbreaks. Thin outlines: locations where it has had mixed results. No outline: too few past outbreaks to judge.](figures/risk_map.png){width=88%}

## `r m$headers$relative`

[DESCRIPTION OF FIGURE 2.]^[Compared with the model's forecasts for the same two-month-ahead window made between `r m$relative$history_start_text` and `r m$relative$history_end_text`, and in earlier monthly memos. Only medium- and high-risk locations are compared. `r m$relative$gap_note`]

![For each medium- or high-risk location, how long ago the model last forecast risk this high.](figures/relative_map.png){width=88%}

## `r m$headers$countries`

[DESCRIPTION OF TABLE 1.]^[Country chances combine the location forecasts, allowing for outbreaks in nearby locations tending to happen together (a Gaussian copula fitted to past outbreaks). Across all countries they add up to `r formatC(m$countries$expected_countries, format = "f", digits = 2)`, the expected number of countries with a recorded outbreak in the period. Chances for very small countries are less reliable. "High-risk locations" counts high-risk hexagons, with those where the model has a good track record in brackets. "Track record" is how well the model forecast past outbreaks in that country.]

```{r}
#| label: tbl-countries
#| tbl-cap: "Countries with the highest chance that at least one Rift Valley fever outbreak is recorded in the forecast period."
knitr::kable(m$countries$table, align = c("r", "l", rep("r", ncol(m$countries$table) - 3), "l"))
```
